title: Hidden pieces & claims
blurb: Face-down cards, claiming a piece type, and claim locking.

steps.say: In Bluff Chess your seven back-rank pieces are face-down cards. You can see what each one really is; your opponent sees only a card back. Their cards show only a red back to you. Pawns and kings are always face-up.
Moving a face-down piece is a claim: you announce what it is. Your b1 card really is a knight. Move it to c3 and claim Knight.
steps.hint: Click the b1 card, click c3, then choose Knight.
steps.success: The badge in the card's corner shows your claim. The Professor could have called it, but he passed.

steps.say: Claims lock: that card is now a Knight for the rest of the game and must keep moving like one. Move it again: any knight move.
steps.hint: Click the card on c3. It can only move like a knight now.
steps.success: Good. A locked claim tells your opponent something, so claim with care.

steps.say: Your opponent's claims show the same way, as a badge in the corner of their cards. The claim tracker beside the board counts them. If more cards claim a type than can exist, someone is lying. Next: catching liars.
